applies_to: Bracketed numeric markers keyed to a numbered reference list: '[1]', '[2, 4, 7]', '[4]-[6]'. Bracketed markers are detected in every document, unlike parenthesised numerals — a bracketed integer group has almost no competing meaning in prose.

cases.text: An earlier architecture achieved the same throughput [1].

cases.note: One marker, three references, one span — the numbered family's version of the author-date grouping case.
A range names every reference in it. Leaving it as an endpoint pair would mark the references between them unused, which is a reported finding, not a silent gap.
cases.text: The surveyed systems [4-6] all use the same encoding.

cases.note: Two markers, not one group: each keeps its own span, so a reviewer sent to either lands on that marker rather than on the pair.
cases.text: Earlier results [1], [2] agree on the bound.

cases.note: Some journals separate a group with semicolons. Same marker, same split.
cases.text: Two follow-up studies [7; 8] repeated the measurement.

cases.note: Extraction wraps lines wherever the source PDF did, so a real marker lands at the start of a line routinely. This is why the notes-list exclusion is paragraph-initial rather than line-initial.
cases.text:
The effect was first reported in
[12], and confirmed later.

cases.note: An endnotes section sits after the bibliography and so survives into the body text the artifact keeps. Every note opens with the marker shape this family looks for; counting them would invent a second occurrence of every cited reference.
cases.text:
The measurement is described elsewhere [3].

[1] Details of the calibration procedure.

[2] The apparatus was replaced mid-study.

cases.note: A group naming the same reference twice is a typo, not two citations. Deduplicating inside the group keeps 'cited N times' honest without hiding the marker.
cases.text: The same source is listed twice here [5, 5].

cases.note: Where the numbered family puts a locator: inside the marker, not after it. The whole span is digits-and-separators plus a page reference, so a group test that does not account for the locator rejects the marker outright — this manuscript would lose every citation it gave a page number to, which is the highest-cost failure the module has.
cases.text: The argument is put most directly in one passage [3, p. 14].

cases.note: The same shape with a section locator and a multi-reference group, so the locator is dropped without taking the second reference with it.
cases.text: Both treatments are given there [7, 8, Sec. 2].

cases.note: The counterpart that keeps the locator allowance from becoming a hole: dropping the locator has to leave a reference behind, or there is nothing to cite.
cases.text: The passage quoted above [p. 14] makes the point.
